sources.title: Surah Aal Imran 3:97 (Quran.com)
sources.supports: Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by those able to make the journey.

sources.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:196 (Quran.com)
sources.supports: Complete Hajj and Umrah for Allah; a sacrifice that is easy for the one who combines Umrah with Hajj.

sources.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:197 (Quran.com)
sources.supports: Hajj in well-known months, with no obscenity, wickedness or quarrelling.

sources.title: Surah Al-Hajj 22:27 (Quran.com)
sources.supports: The call to people to perform Hajj, who come on foot and by every distant road.

sources.title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 889
sources.supports: Hajj is Arafah; whoever reaches Jam in the night before Fajr attended; the days of Mina are three, leaving after two or staying are both without sin. Hadith text verified against the open hadith-api dataset mirroring the Sunnah.com collection; Sunnah.com itself returned a Cloudflare 403 to automated retrieval.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1521
sources.supports: Whoever performs Hajj for Allah without sexual relations or sin returns as if newly born. Hadith text verified against the open hadith-api dataset mirroring the Sunnah.com collection; Sunnah.com itself returned a Cloudflare 403 to automated retrieval.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1755
sources.supports: People were ordered to make Tawaf al-Wada their last act before leaving Makkah, except menstruating women. Hadith text verified against the open hadith-api dataset mirroring the Sunnah.com collection; Sunnah.com itself returned a Cloudflare 403 to automated retrieval.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1773
sources.supports: The reward of an accepted Hajj is nothing except Paradise. Hadith text verified against the open hadith-api dataset mirroring the Sunnah.com collection; Sunnah.com itself returned a Cloudflare 403 to automated retrieval.

review.notes: All eight sources retrieved and read from saved files; quotes match. Sunnah.com blocked automated access, so hadith were verified via the open hadith-api dataset. Operational rules (permits, health) are deliberately not asserted beyond directing readers to official sources. Contested juristic details are flagged as scholar-dependent rather than stated as universal. Original metadata (title, date, author, hero) is preserved by the publisher.
